title: The Next Eight Weeks Could Change America Forever | Robert Pape
summary: A political scientist warns that a renewed US or Israeli strike on Iran is likely after the US midterms, that Iran will retaliate harder, and that the war interacts dangerously with US domestic politics.

assertions.quote: the odds will will grow after November 3rd and then they'll get to about 70 75% by the time we get to January 3rd

verdicts.note: A near-term forecast about a war in progress; no independent forecast record is available to judge it yet.

assertions.quote: Iran uh is going to push back in decisive powerful ways and some of that is killing leaders

verdicts.note: Iran under-retaliated in 2020 and 2024 but, by contemporary reports, struck Gulf bases and shipping after the 2026 attack; its next response is uncertain.

assertions.quote: there is no economic blockade since World War I that without a ground war has produced major concessions

verdicts.note: Sanctions research finds economic pressure alone seldom wins major concessions, though the coding of some cases is disputed.

assertions.quote: for Trump, the more he loses, the more the GOP goes down, the bigger the incentive to go big and escalate against Iran
It's because it's easy in. It's easy in and then it gets harder and harder once they're in.

verdicts.note: Vietnam, Afghanistan and Iraq fit the pattern, but many interventions stayed limited; it is a tendency, not a rule.
Braumoeller: leaders make a series of decisions that each seem reasonable and reversible, which can lead to a catastrophic war nobody intended.

assertions.quote: I think Iran's going to get a nuclear weapon and I think Israel's nuclear forces will deter Iran.

verdicts.note: The 2025 and 2026 strikes set back Iran's programme and whether it decides to build a weapon is not known.
XPT forecasters named Iran the most likely new nuclear power by 2030 and 2050, with a median of one new nuclear state by 2030.
85% of surveyed strategists expect new nuclear states by 2036 and 66% of them name Iran (about 56% of all respondents), despite the 2025 strikes.

assertions.quote: when it kicked off for the first time since World War II, it did not get majority public support.

verdicts.note: Polling on the 2026 war is not independently checkable here; earlier wars such as Iraq in 2003 did start with majority support.

assertions.quote: this would lead to the rise of oil prices and the rise of gas prices in the United States
